_comment: §7's mock budget. A RATCHET: `ratchet` may only SHRINK, and the gate fails in
BOTH directions -- beating it without lowering it is a finding too, because an
unlowered ratchet is a ceiling nobody is holding.
`inventory` is the count's own contents, because a bare number cannot tell a
repaired use from a renamed one: 21 and 21 look identical when one call was
removed and another introduced the same day. Duplicates are KEPT, so the count
and the inventory are the same artifact.
Every remaining entry is legitimate and is COUNTED rather than exempted by name.
A name-based exemption is a list standing in for the artifact, and the number is
the whole point of a ratchet:
* monkeypatch.setenv/delenv -- the ENVIRONMENT has no port. It is process
state, and setting it is how ServiceConfig.from_environment() is driven at all.
* monkeypatch.setattr(socket, 'socket', ...) -- the assertion IS that the
standard-library call never happens while the container graph is built.
There is no collaborator here to fake.
* monkeypatch.setenv('REDIS_PORT', '1') -- points the kit at a port
nothing listens on, to prove the refusal names a remedy. The port is a TCP
endpoint, not an object; making it unreachable is the only honest way to
reach that branch.
* monkeypatch.setattr(entrypoint.uvicorn, 'run', ...) -- the assertion is that
run() is reached with the CONFIGURED port and host. A server that really binds
proves nothing about which port it was told to bind, and an ASGI server is not
a collaborator this package has a port for.
* monkeypatch.setattr(container, 'AwsSecretsManagerSecrets'/'build_secrets', ...)
-- the question is whether the composition ROOT constructs the credential
adapter at all, and on which branch. Passing the fake through `secrets=` would
bypass the one expression under test, so the construction has to be OBSERVED.
RE-BASELINED 2026-09-15 FROM 14 TO 21, and this is a re-baseline rather than a
raise. Attribution as SETS, never as totals: 7 NEW, 0 GONE.
The 14 was measured on a tree that could not see five of the seven. This gate and
this file arrived on one side of a merge; `tests/unit/test_main_entrypoint.py`
arrived on the other, and `git cat-file -e` on each parent says so -- the budget
is ABSENT at HEAD and the entrypoint test is ABSENT at MERGE_HEAD. So no ratchet
that anyone was holding went up; two populations that had never been measured
together were joined, and 21 is the first measurement of the joined one.
NEW (7):
5x unit/test_main_entrypoint.py -- 2 setenv, 1 delenv, 2 uvicorn.run setattr.
Present at HEAD, absent at MERGE_HEAD, so the 14 never counted them.
2x unit/test_container.py::monkeypatch.setattr -- the credential-seam arms added
here: one records which region the root builds an AWS client for (and that a
SQLite service builds none), one explodes if the `secrets or build_secrets(...)`
default is evaluated eagerly.
GONE (0). Nothing was repaired away under cover of the move.
LOWERED 2026-09-18 FROM 21 TO 20 (the ORM slice). Attribution as
SETS, never as totals, because 21 and 20 cannot tell a repaired use from a renamed
one: 2 NEW, 2 GONE, and one file's count fell by one.
NEW (2):
1x unit/test_container_database.py::monkeypatch.setattr -- the socket guard, moved
with the file when test_container_db_backend.py was rewritten around
DATABASE_URL. It is the same assertion, not an additional one.
1x unit/test_config.py::monkeypatch.delenv -- the new arm proving a MISSING
DATABASE_URL is refused naming the variable. The environment has no port; a test
of what happens when a variable is absent has to make it absent.
GONE (2):
1x unit/test_container_db_backend.py::monkeypatch.setattr -- the file, deleted with
the db_backend selector it tested.
1x unit/test_config.py::monkeypatch.setenv -- three separate setenv call sites in
test_from_environment_reads_overrides became one dict loop, which is also how
DATABASE_URL was added to it without buying a new call site.
LOWERED BY ONE MORE:
1x unit/test_main_entrypoint.py::monkeypatch.setenv -- two call sites became one
dict loop, for the same reason: importing main.py now needs DATABASE_URL, and a
third setenv line would have demanded the ratchet be RAISED, which is the one
thing a ratchet must never do.
ZERO uses of unittest.mock / MagicMock, and that is the half the ratchet is
really holding.
LOWERED 2026-09-25 FROM 16 TO 15. Attribution as SETS: 0 NEW, 1 GONE.
The tree had drifted to 17 before this: 65d50d6 added a third
unit/test_main_entrypoint.py::monkeypatch.setattr(entrypoint.uvicorn, 'run', ...) for the
grace-ceiling arm and left this file at 16, so the gate was red on develop. The three
interceptions were one decision written three times; they are now one `served` fixture
that each arm reads, so the file carries ONE setattr where the inventory recorded two.
GONE (1):
1x unit/test_main_entrypoint.py::monkeypatch.setattr -- folded into the `served` fixture.
Each arm still asserts its own keyword (port, host, timeout_graceful_shutdown), and
breaking any one of them in main.py reddens exactly that arm.
RAISED 2026-09-27 FROM 15 TO 16 (the Lambda dispatch change). Attribution as SETS: 1 NEW, 0 GONE.
NEW (1):
1x unit/test_lambda_dispatch.py::monkeypatch.setitem -- ONE call site in the
`fake_main_module` fixture, shared by all four tests that need a dispatchable
module. `sys.modules` has no port: `lambda_dispatch.mount_non_http_dispatch()`
resolves the target module through `importlib.import_module`, and a real
`<name>_main.py` this template does not itself emit (comms-core/comms-email
each author their own) is not a fixture this repository can construct as a
fake adapter. Injecting a `ModuleType` into `sys.modules` is the same shape
as the socket-guard and uvicorn-run interceptions already in this budget: there
is no collaborator here to fake, only the import mechanism to observe.
